dedupe_keys.name: ambulance decision game queueing markov chain and game theoretic model of the ambulance and emergency department interface

description: Ambulance Decision Game is a Python library that models what happens when ambulances queue to hand patients over at hospital emergency departments, and how departments and the ambulance service behave strategically when they face waiting-time targets. The producer is Michalis Panayides at Cardiff University; the method is published in the European Journal of Operational Research (2023) as a game theoretic model of behavioural gaming at the interface between emergency medical services and emergency departments. Coverage is generic: the model is parameterised by arrival and service rates, not tied to one region. It contains a discrete-event simulation of a queue with two waiting spaces where ambulance patients can be blocked, the equivalent Markov chain for exact results, and a three-player game between two departments and an ambulance distributor that finds equilibrium routing. The code is available on GitHub and PyPI under the free MIT licence, with a release archived on Zenodo. Caveats: the last commit was in December 2022, the models assume stationary Markovian arrivals, and no real-world data set is bundled. Simulation uses: studying ambulance handover delays and their knock-on effect on response capacity, testing capacity or target changes at emergency departments, and representing hospital blocking in wider emergency response models. Related records: the NHSX ambulance simulation (model-ambulance-des-nhsx) and OpenEMS (model-openems-ambulance-deployment) cover ambulance dispatch and location.
inputs: Arrival rates of ambulance and other patients
Service rates and numbers of servers in each emergency department
Capacities of the waiting spaces (ambulance holding and department)
name: Ambulance Decision Game: queueing, Markov chain and game theoretic model of the ambulance and emergency department interface
outputs: Waiting-time and blocking-time distributions from simulation and Markov chain
Equilibrium strategies for two emergency departments and an ambulance distributor
